Alamance County by the numbers

What does the Alamance County Register of Deeds do for a home seller?

This is where the deed that passes title to your buyer gets recorded, and where the permanent index of deeds, deeds of trust, plats and easements for the whole county is kept. Staff here only record. Under North Carolina law they may not practice law, so they will not hand out legal forms or advise you on what a document does.

Graham is the seat and Burlington the largest community. Properties in Burlington, Mebane, Elon, Haw River and the rest of the county's thirteen townships all go through this one office.

The front counter keeps weekday hours of 8:00 to 5:00, but the last submission for recording is 4:30, a cutoff set when the county adopted G.S. 153A-94(b) in August 2013. The office phone menu has separate options for recording help, for earlier recorded documents, and for vital records.

What are the recording fees at the Alamance County Register of Deeds?

The published schedule below shows a deed at $26 through page 15, with $4 for every page after. A deed of trust is priced on a longer base. The deed of trust figure was reset effective October 1, 2016.

Recording and copy fees listed by the Alamance County Register of Deeds
ItemFee
Deed$26 for pages 1 to 15, then $4 per page
Deed of trust or mortgage$64 for pages 1 to 35, then $4 per page
Multiple documents in one filing$10 added to the recording fee
Non-standard document$25 added to the recording fee
Plat$21
Certified copy$5 for the first page, $2 per added page
Uncertified copy$0.25 per page

Vital record fees on the same schedule, such as marriage licenses and certified birth, death and marriage certificates, are cash or money order only. Ask the office which payment types it accepts for recording before you go.

How much is the North Carolina excise tax on a deed?

North Carolina taxes each conveyance at $1.00 per $500 of value, with a part-payment of $500 counted whole. The transferor pays it to the register of deeds ahead of recording, under G.S. 105-228.30. For a parcel in more than one county, payment goes where most of the value lies.

The register remits the proceeds to the county finance officer. One half stays with the county general fund, and the state receives the rest, after refunds and the county's collection allowance. Timber deeds are covered by the same statute.

You will not find this tax on the county's fee schedule, because it is a state levy, separate from the recording charge. Your settlement attorney reads the consideration off the deed and collects the tax alongside the fee. Ask to see the figure on your settlement statement before the closing date.

What formatting rules must a deed meet in Alamance County?

Paper deeds must satisfy G.S. 161-14(b), which the county restates on its recording page. A deed that fails still gets recorded, for an extra $25.

  • Sheets of 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • Three blank inches above the first page text, with half an inch minimum elsewhere on page one and on all edges of later pages.
  • Black print on white paper, with nine point as the smallest legible font. Pen is allowed for blanks and corrections.
  • Printing on one side only.
  • The instrument's title at the top of page one, under the margin.

Plats follow a separate rule: mylar only, cut to 18 by 24 inches. Enclose a stamped self-addressed envelope sized for the recorded document.

What happens to the deed after it is recorded?

Staff stamp each instrument with the day and hour it arrived and record in arrival order. The statute gives the office up to 30 days to finish indexing. Keep the book and page number the county assigns, because it is how you will refer to the document later.

A step that surprises some sellers comes first. Deeds recorded since May 2, 2011 (timber deeds and releases excepted) pass through the county Tax Department for a delinquent tax certification. Overdue county tax stalls recording until it is paid, so request a payoff early.

Electronic recording has been available since November 2015 for everything but plats, so your attorney can submit through a vendor. After recording, Land Records at the Tax Department revises the owner name and mailing address. Straight sales move quicker than splits. Call with your book and page number if nothing changes after several weeks.

Which other Alamance County offices touch a house sale?

A sale here usually involves three offices besides this one, and each keeps a different slice of the record.

  • Tax Department, Land Records: at 124 W. Elm St. in Graham, phone (336) 228-1312. It owns the parcel's owner name, mailing address and tax map, and its staff want the book and page number of any recorded deed when you call about a change.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: holds estate filings and court orders, which establish who owns a house after a death or a court proceeding.
  • North Carolina Secretary of State: holds business filings. A merger, name change or dissolution alters how a company-owned parcel is listed.

Names on the county record follow the recorded deed letter for letter. A misspelling that appears on the deed itself needs a corrected document recorded here, and a lawyer can prepare it. A marriage or court-ordered name change does not alter the owner name unless a new document is recorded.

Tax bills are mailed in July and fall due September 1, so changing a mailing address before July keeps the bill from going astray after you sell.

How do I search or copy Alamance County land records?

Search recorded deeds by name through the office's online search, and go to the office itself for certified copies. The website cautions that online records are unofficial, and the paper records in the office are the official ones.

  • Certified copies: $5 for page one, $2 for each page after it.
  • Plain copies: $0.25 a page.
  • Owner, mailing address and legal description: the Tax Department's property record search.
  • Tax maps are drawn for assessment and are not surveys. Use a licensed surveyor and the recorded plat for any boundary question.

If you are paying off a mortgage, have the lender record the release, since cancellation of a deed of trust is itself a recorded instrument.

What local facts affect a deed transfer in Alamance County?

QuickFacts shows 83,187 housing units for July 2025 and 70,062 households in 2020 to 2024, at 2.44 people each. Nearly nine in ten residents (89.3%) lived at the same address a year before, and 28.7% of adults over 25 hold a bachelor's degree or better. With the July 2025 estimate of 186,177 running 8.6% over the April 2020 base, conveyances keep arriving.

The county dates to 1849, carved from Orange County, and takes its name from the creek where the Battle of Alamance was fought on May 16, 1771. When title runs through an estate, the Clerk of Superior Court files the estate papers and this office records the deeds the heirs or the court sign.

More questions about Alamance County, NC Register of Deeds

What is the last time of day to record a deed in Alamance County?

Documents must come in by 4:30 p.m. The doors stay open until 5:00, yet the recording cutoff arrives half an hour earlier under G.S. 153A-94(b).

Who pays North Carolina's deed excise tax?

The transferor does, ahead of recording. G.S. 105-228.30 sets $1.00 per $500 of value, rounding any part of $500 up.

What does it cost to record a deed here?

A deed costs $26 through page 15, then $4 per added page. Documents that miss the formatting rules carry a $25 surcharge.

Is electronic recording offered in Alamance County?

Yes, for every document except plats, since November 2015. Closing attorneys normally submit through a recording vendor.

Why did my deed have to go to the Tax Department first?

Deeds recorded after May 2, 2011, other than timber deeds and releases, need delinquent tax certification from the county Tax Department before recording. Unpaid county tax must be cleared first.

Where does Alleghany County record a deed?

A deed for Alleghany County land goes to the Register of Deeds, 348 South Main Street, Sparta, NC 28675. Call 336-372-4342 to reach the office. Staff are on site until 5:00 p.m., yet nothing is accepted for recording once the clock passes 4:30 p.m.

Alleghany sits in the Blue Ridge Mountains of northwestern North Carolina and was cut out of Ashe County by the 1858-1859 session of the legislature. The county seat is Sparta, and the same administration building that houses the register also holds the tax office. That matters for sellers, because a deed here cannot be recorded without a paper from the tax side of the building.

The register is a recording office. Staff explain county requirements and nothing more. Drafting and legal advice belong to your closing attorney. For ownership lookups by street address, the county points callers to its E-911 and Mapping office at 336-372-7920 instead of the register.

Which items does the Sparta office check on a deed?

The county's checklist asks for a notarized signature, a named drafter, the buyer's address, a tax certification, and payment of excise tax and fees.

  • The grantor's signature must be properly notarized.
  • Deeds and deeds of trust written in North Carolina must name the person who drafted them on the first page.
  • The grantee's address goes on the first page so the tax office knows where to send bills.
  • The tax certification from the Alleghany County tax administrator must be attached before recording.
  • The grantor pays the real estate excise tax when the deed is recorded.
  • Recording fees are paid before any document is accepted.

Page layout is checked as well. The county wants legal or letter size sheets, a roomy blank band across the top of page one, dark print no smaller than 10 points, one-sided pages, and the instrument title near the top. Pen is fine for blanks and corrections. A deed that falls short still gets recorded, with a $25.00 surcharge added to the normal charges.

Why does Alleghany County ask for a tax certification with every deed?

The county requires a tax certification form to accompany all deeds, and the register's FAQ repeats that a deed cannot be recorded without one. The tax office issues the form, and its phone number is 336-372-8291.

The certification rests on G.S. 105-361(a), which says the tax collector must furnish a written certificate on request showing the current and prior-year taxes, penalties, interest and costs that are a lien on a parcel. The county tax office FAQ goes further and says taxes on a parcel must be paid in full before a deed for it can be recorded. The request has to name the person in whose name the land was listed for each year. Request the form early, since an open bill can stall the recording.

In practice a seller should expect every county charge on the parcel, such as the solid waste fee and fire district tax, to be cleared at the table. Confirm whether your closing attorney or you will request the certificate.

What does recording a deed in Alleghany County cost?

A standard deed runs $26.00 through page 15 with $4.00 for every page beyond that, and the seller owes excise tax on top. The table gathers what the county prints and the statewide amounts it follows.

Alleghany County recording charges (county FAQ and checklist, G.S. 161-10)
ItemCharge as printed

Excise tax, paid by the grantor$2.00 for every $1,000 of price
Nonstandard document add-on$25.00

Certified copy$5.00 for page one, $2.00 per later page

Statute G.S. 105-228.30 states the same tax as one dollar per $500 or part of $500 and puts it on the seller. A mortgage-type document carries a higher base fee, which the lender's closing agent handles.

What do federal numbers show for Alleghany homes?

QuickFacts lists 11,479 people for July 2025, compared with 10,888 counted in 2020, across 234.84 square miles of land.

  • Housing units: 8,035 in 2025, against 5,177 households for 2020 to 2024.
  • Homeowners as a share of occupied homes: 74.4 percent.
  • Typical value of an owner's home: $214,800.
  • Median gross rent: $675.
  • People aged 65 or more: 31.4 percent.
  • Median household income: $47,172.

Housing units outnumber households by a wide margin, which fits a county with many second homes and seasonal cabins. The older age profile also means plenty of heirs end up selling a parent's house, and for those cases the deed from an estate has to meet the same recording rules described above.

How are Alleghany County property taxes set and when is the next revaluation?

The county tax rate printed for fiscal year 2026-27 is 0.597 per $100 of value, with a $108 residential solid waste fee and a fire district rate that depends on where the house sits. Real estate is reappraised at least every eight years, and Alleghany's last revaluation took effect in 2021.

Its successor starts January 1, 2027. The tax office reports that data collection began in May 2025, that notices will be mailed in late winter or early spring 2027, and that the county holds about 14,736 parcels in the revaluation update. Its presentation shows what changed on individual sales since 2021. One Sparta single-family house from 1968, assessed at $94,100 in 2021, sold in May 2025 for $226,420, which the county lists as a 141 percent increase. Those are single examples, and the county says values moved by different amounts in different areas.

Fire district rates, per $100 of value as printed:

  • Cherry Lane: .04
  • Laurel Springs: .07
  • Sparta: .03
  • Glade Creek: .07
  • Piney Creek: .06

Is there an early-payment discount in Alleghany County?

Yes. Current-year taxes paid between August 1 and August 31 earn a 2 percent discount. Bills left past January 5 pick up 2 percent interest on January 6, plus 0.75 percent at the start of each later month.

Property and improvements must be listed by January 31. The county tax office also handles the exclusions and exemptions the state offers: religious, educational, charitable, elderly or disabled, disabled veteran and farm present use value. For the age-65 or disabled exclusion, 2026 income may not exceed $38,800. Disabled veterans can exclude the first $45,000 of value with no age or income test.

File with the county assessor; the state accepts forms through June 1. If you sell a house that carries one of these programs, tell the buyer's attorney, since the circuit breaker deferral can bring back up to three years of deferred tax when the property is transferred.

How should an Alleghany County owner prepare before closing?

Start with the tax certification, then confirm the deed details and the money. A short order of operations keeps the recording on schedule.

  • Call the tax office at 336-372-8291 for the certification form and the amount owed on the parcel.
  • Check that the deed names the drafter and gives the buyer's mailing address on page one.
  • Arrange for the excise tax and recording fee to be paid at closing, before the 4:30 p.m. recording cutoff.
  • Ask the Clerk of Court at 336-372-3900 how to look up judgments or mechanics liens that could attach to the land.
  • Order a certified copy of the recorded deed afterward if the buyer's lender needs one.

Sellers with a house that needs repairs, liens or inherited title questions can still sell as-is. Recording works the same way for every house; the payoff amounts are what differ.

More questions about Alleghany County, NC Register of Deeds

What time does the Alleghany County Register of Deeds stop accepting documents?

Its cutoff is 4:30 p.m. every day, though the building stays open until 5:00 p.m. Find it at 348 South Main Street in Sparta, phone 336-372-4342.

Is a tax certification required for an Alleghany deed?

Yes. The county says a tax certification form must accompany all deeds. Get it from the Alleghany County Tax Office at 336-372-8291, and expect any unpaid property tax on the parcel to be settled first.

Who owes the deed stamp tax on an Alleghany sale?

The seller, as grantor. The county prints $2.00 per $1,000 of price, paid at recording, which equals the one dollar per $500 in state law.

What does a copy of a recorded Alleghany deed cost?

An in-person plain copy is $.05 a page, and mail requests work too. Certified copies are priced by statute at $5.00 for the opening page and $2.00 for every further page.

When does the next Alleghany County revaluation take effect?

January 1, 2027. Notices of new values are due to be mailed in late winter or early spring 2027, and owners can contest a value before the county appeal board. The prior reset was in 2021.

How do I get a deed into the Avery County records?

Deeds reach the Avery County registry three ways: at the counter, through the mail, or by electronic recording. The counter is staffed Monday to Friday from 8 a.m. until 4:30 in the afternoon, but the last filing of the day is taken at 4:15.

Land records for all 247 square miles of the county sit here, and a public search website shows index entries and document images. Staff only record. Because North Carolina bars them from practicing law, they will not hand out legal forms, coach you on drafting, or comment on what a filed paper does to title; a closing attorney does.

The county tax office adds a useful reminder on its own page: the legal description of a parcel comes from the recorded deed, and the tax maps are meant for valuation only. If the map and the deed disagree, the deed controls.

What fees does the Avery registry charge?

The office's schedule sets a general instrument at $26.00 through 15 pages, and a deed of trust at $64.00 through 35 pages, with $4.00 for each extra page of either. Sale excise tax is separate.

Avery County Register of Deeds fee schedule, as the office prints it (G.S. 161-10)
Document or serviceFee
Deed or other general instrument$26.00 up to 15 pages, plus $4.00 per extra page
Deed of trust$64.00 up to 35 pages, plus $4.00 per extra page
Plat$21.00 per page, 18 by 24 inch only
Excise tax$1 per $500 of the price
Satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trustNo fee
Certified copy$5.00 opening page, $2.00 per following page
Nonstandard document$25.00 extra

Two smaller charges are easy to miss. A document that names more than 20 distinct parties to be indexed adds $2.00 for each name past the twentieth, and a later instrument that refers to more than one earlier recorded instrument costs $25.00 for each additional reference.

Who pays the excise tax when an Avery County house sells?

The seller pays it. G.S. 105-228.30 assigns it to the transferor, who pays the registry first.

The tax is $1 per $500 of price, counting any leftover portion as a full $500. The money is split between county government and the state. Because it follows the contract price, the amount is known as soon as you sign a contract, and it should appear on the settlement statement.

  • Seller: excise tax, plus any recording charge for a release of the old mortgage, which is normally free to record.
  • Buyer: recording fee for the new deed and the lender's deed of trust.
  • Either side: nonstandard document charge if the paperwork does not meet format rules.

A contract can shift costs, so read the settlement statement before signing.

How does recording affect who owns the property?

Under G.S. 47-18 a transfer only binds lien creditors and later buyers once it is registered in the county of the land, and priority runs by recording time.

That is why Avery County closings end with a recording and not just a signing. A deed that sits unrecorded in a drawer leaves the buyer exposed. The register's office also holds the paperwork that clears the seller's side, such as the satisfaction of a prior deed of trust, so a payoff letter and a recorded cancellation should both show up in the index.

Keep the recorded copy and the recording stamp with your closing file, since they are the proof that the transfer took effect on a given date.

What kind of county is Avery, and who lives in its houses?

Avery County sits high in the northwestern mountains, bordered by Tennessee and by Watauga, Caldwell, Burke and Mitchell counties. Its seat, Newland, stands at 3,589 feet, which the county calls the highest county seat in the eastern United States, and the county straddles the eastern continental divide near 4,000 feet.

The county names Colonel Waightstill Avery of Morganton as its namesake. Winters are real here. The county reports an average of 58 inches of snow and temperatures about ten degrees cooler than Asheville or Charlotte, and the ski slopes stay covered from mid-November through March. Seven towns sit inside the county: Banner Elk, Beech Mountain, Crossnore, Elk Park, Newland, Seven Devils and Sugar Mountain.

Newland began as "Old Fields of Toe", a broad flat valley at the headwaters of the Toe River. The county's tax records divide the land into eight townships (Altamont, Banner Elk, Beech Mountain, Cranberry, Linville, Roaring Creek, Toe River and Wilson's Creek) and ten fire districts. When you ask the tax office for a payoff, give the township or town along with the parcel details so the right rates are applied.

Federal housing and population figures:

  • People: 18,110 as of July 2025.
  • Housing units: 14,597 in 2025 against 6,791 households for 2020 to 2024.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 83.0 percent.
  • Median owner-occupied home value: $265,800.
  • Median gross rent: $773.
  • Residents 65 and over: 26.9 percent.

More than twice as many housing units as households points to a large stock of vacation homes, which is worth keeping in mind when a house has been empty through winters.

How do Avery County taxes reach a closing?

Avery County's tax office bills real and personal property under two divisions, assessment and collections, and its rate page lists a 2025 county rate of 0.335 plus a 0.065 fire rate for a total of 0.40. No unit appears beside the numbers, so have the tax office confirm how they apply to a bill.

The current values date from the January 1, 2022 revaluation, with notices mailed that March. Tax bills follow state timing: due September 1, interest starting after January 5. Avery's listing period runs through January, and the county told owners that taxpayers carry the duty to list even if no form arrives.

The county tax office phone is 828-733-8214 for assessment and 828-733-8228 for collections. Before closing, call both offices and pass the figures to the title attorney.

What checks help an Avery County seller before recording day?

Confirm the pieces below a few days ahead and the recording will go through at the first attempt.

  • Have the deed drafted by an attorney and notarized, with the preparer's name on it.
  • Print on white paper in a legible font with a clear top margin so the nonstandard charge is avoided.
  • Bring a plat only on 18 by 24 inch sheets if a subdivision map is part of the transaction.
  • Plan to reach the register before the 4:15 p.m. recording cutoff.
  • Search the online index for the property to see any recorded easements or old deeds of trust that still show open.

If you hold a house you inherited or one that needs repairs, the same recording steps apply. Sellers who want a quick, as-is sale still go through the same register, and the same tax and excise tax charges follow the contract price.

More questions about Avery County, NC Register of Deeds

When can I record in Avery County?

Weekdays the office keeps 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. hours, and filings are accepted until 4:15 p.m. Counter, mail and electronic submissions are all taken.

What will Avery County charge me to record my deed?

A general instrument is $26.00 through page 15 and $4.00 for each page beyond. Excise tax is extra at $1 per $500, and a nonstandard paper adds $25.00.

Is there a fee to record the release of a mortgage in Avery County?

No. The register's schedule lists satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trust as no fee, which matches the statewide fee statute.

Can the Avery County register of deeds give legal advice about my deed?

No. Staff cannot practice law, so they will not supply forms, show you how to fill one in, or explain its effect. An attorney can.

Who gives me a tax payoff figure in Avery County?

Call the Avery County tax office. Dial 828-733-8214 for assessment or 828-733-8228 for collections. Request this year's balance and any earlier balance for the parcel.

How do I reach the Beaufort County registry?

Walk in at 112 W 2nd Street, Washington, NC 27889, or write to P.O. Box 514. Staff keep weekday hours of 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., stop taking filings at 4:45 p.m., and answer at 252-946-2323.

The county page cites G.S. 84-4 and 84-5 to explain that staff cannot help prepare legal papers. Arrive with a finished deed from your lawyer.

What must a Beaufort deed show on its face?

The office's recording guide mixes state standards with local steps.

  • Letter or legal paper, printed on one side in legible type of 9 points or larger on white stock.
  • Three blank inches at the head of page one, and half-inch margins elsewhere.
  • The kind of instrument written at the top of the first page.
  • A preparer's name on every deed and deed of trust.
  • On a deed, the buyer's address plus a note on whether the seller lived there as a primary residence.
  • A sign-off from Land Records on deeds and certain maps before filing.

Paper that misses the format rules can still be filed, subject to a $25.00 nonstandard fee, and the register may waive that fee when only the type size is short and the text is legible. Surveys and plats, along with Torrens documents, are not accepted electronically, so they go in on paper.

Why does a Beaufort County deed go through Land Records first?

The county ties its mapping and tax listing to recorded deeds, so Land Records looks at a deed before the register files it. That office is at 220 N. Market Street in Washington and the phone is 252-946-6591.

Land Records manages the county's parcel mapping and GIS databases, applies recorded documents such as wills and deeds when it administers tax listings, and helps the public and professionals with record reviews. For a seller, the takeaway is to drop the deed there early, because the register's guide puts that approval ahead of recording.

Beaufort also posts a resolution on tax certification for deeds among the register's downloads. Ask the register or the tax collector whether a certificate is needed for your closing, because that rule is set locally.

What are the costs to record in Beaufort County?

State law in G.S. 161-10 fixes most amounts, and the county posts its own schedule file. The table pairs those amounts with the nonstandard charge from the office guide.

Recording charges that apply in Beaufort County (state statute G.S. 161-10 and the register's recording guide)

Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 up to 35 pages, then $4.00 a page

Certified copy$5.00 for the first sheet, $2.00 for each more
Nonstandard document$25.00

Excise tax is a separate line: the seller pays a dollar per $500 of price at the registry, and the county retains half. For anything out of the ordinary, request the office's current schedule.

How does the Beaufort County fraud alert protect owners?

Beaufort's registry emails you, at no charge, when a recorded document matches a name you enroll. Each email address can list five names, and only filings made after signup count.

The office explains the reason for the service plainly: it must record any document that is properly executed and presented with payment, and it cannot know whether a signature is forged. Nothing can be removed from the official records after recording, even if a document is proven fraudulent. An owner who suspects fraud should call the sheriff's office at 252-946-7111 and speak to an attorney, because the register has no power to reverse the filing.

A name you enroll can be your own or a relative's, which suits owners of land they rarely visit.

What is Beaufort County like for a seller?

Beaufort County is a coastal plain county built around the Pamlico River, with 88,000 acres of water and a long border on the Pamlico Sound. Washington, the county seat, sits where the Tar and Pamlico rivers meet.

The county was formed in 1705 as Pamptecough Precinct and named in 1712. Bath, founded in 1705, is the oldest town in the state. Seven municipalities lie within it: Aurora, Bath, Belhaven, Chocowinity, Pantego, Washington and Washington Park. Washington once had a busy port and a thriving shipbuilding trade and remains the cultural and economic center, Chocowinity served as a Norfolk Southern railroad hub from 1910, and the waterfronts that used to ship lumber and naval stores have turned more recreational and residential. Census figures:

  • Population: 44,670 in 2025, down from 47,759 at the 2010 census.
  • Land area: 832.74 square miles.
  • Housing units: 25,204 in 2025, with 19,385 households.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 69.5 percent.
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $192,700.
  • Median gross rent: $871.
  • Residents 65 and older: 29.1 percent; veterans: 3,361.

Waterfront and inland parcels do not move together. The county itself notes that property on or near the water has historically changed in value much faster than inland land.

How do Beaufort County taxes interact with a sale?

Bills are issued as of July 1 and fall due September 1, with interest and enforced collection starting if payment is not in by January 5. For real estate, the owner on January 1 is the listing taxpayer and remains responsible until the past due date, whatever the buyer and seller agree at closing.

That is a real trap for a seller. A seller who closes after the bills go out may still get one in the mail, and the county asks that it be sent on to the buyer or returned to the collector. Escrow lenders are not automatic either: the owner must tell the lender the amount and confirm with the collector that payment arrived.

The 2025 revaluation took effect January 1, 2025, and the commissioners set a six-year cycle going forward. Value appeals may be filed from January each year, up to the adjournment of the county review board, typically in mid-April. The county commissioners set county, fire and EMS district rates when the budget is adopted, while town officials set municipal rates. Vehicles are taxed through the NCDMV at tag renewal, not on the real estate bill. The tax collector offers payment plans with a 20 percent down payment, set up in person between January 6 and June 30.

More questions about Beaufort County, NC Register of Deeds

When is the last filing time in Beaufort County?

Filing closes at 4:45 p.m., fifteen minutes before the 5 p.m. weekday close. The office is at 112 W 2nd Street in Washington and can be reached at 252-946-2323.

Does a deed need Land Records approval in Beaufort County?

Yes. The register's recording guide says deeds and some maps must be approved by the Beaufort County Land Records office before recording. Land Records is at 220 N. Market Street, phone 252-946-6591.

Can I record a plat electronically in Beaufort County?

No. The county lists survey maps and plats, along with Torrens documents, as not accepted electronically. Those two are the only document types the county page excludes from electronic recording.

Who pays the tax bill after a Beaufort sale?

The January 1 owner stays responsible until the past due date, regardless of what the buyer and seller arranged at closing, according to the county. Send any notice to the buyer or back to the collector.

Can Beaufort County warn me about filings in my name?

Yes. The register runs a free fraud alert email service. You can enroll five names per email address and receive a notice when a matching document is recorded, but only for documents recorded after signup.

Brunswick County by the numbers

What does the Brunswick County Register of Deeds handle?

This office keeps the land records for Brunswick County. Deeds, deeds of trust, easements, maps, releases and satisfactions all pass through it, and so do marriage licenses, certified copies and oaths. Voters choose the register for a four-year term. The staff can file what you bring but cannot advise you or draft the paper.

Brunswick was carved out in 1764 from parts of Bladen and New Hanover, and the vault still holds grants, indentures and conveyances from that first period. Modern filings include restrictions and covenants, assumed names, UCC statements and powers of attorney next to the steady stream of deeds from coastal home sales.

A seller here ends up at this counter, either in person, by mail or through a title firm. Until the buyer's deed is on the record, the sale is not protected against outside claims, so the practical details below deserve a read before closing day.

Where is the Brunswick County Register of Deeds and what are its hours?

Look for Building I at 75 Courthouse Drive NE, Bolivia, NC 28422. Call 910-253-2690, or the toll-free alternate 877-625-9310; postal mail is addressed to PO Box 87 in Bolivia. Each service keeps its own window.

  • Recording desk: opens 8:30 am, closes 4:30 pm, weekdays.
  • Land and vital records: opens 8:30 am, closes 5 pm, weekdays.
  • Marriage licenses: by appointment, 8:30 am until 4:30 pm.
  • Passports: by appointment, 8:30 am until 3:30 pm.

You can hand a document over at the counter, post it to the box, or ship it by courier to the Courthouse Drive street address. The county holiday calendar applies to the recording desk.

What does Brunswick County require before it will record a deed?

A short county checklist governs what the clerks accept. Only an original, or a certified copy that carries the original signature, can go on the record.

  • The recording fee, paid by check to BCROD, plus a stamped return envelope.
  • The preparer's name and address on page one.
  • Names and addresses of both seller and buyer on the face of the deed.
  • Signatures and a notary seal that reads clearly.
  • The delinquent tax certification step the county lists for all deeds.
  • Excise tax, which the county explains as $2 per $1,000 of the sales price.

Layout counts too. Under G.S. 161-14(b), as the county quotes it, use letter or legal paper, leave a three-inch blank band on page one, keep half-inch margins elsewhere, print in black on white at 9 points or more, and use one side of each sheet. A deed outside those limits is still accepted, with a $25 charge added.

How much will filing a deed in Brunswick County run?

Two sources set the price: a statewide schedule and the county's copy rates. The lines below follow the wording of the official pages.

Charges tied to a Brunswick County deed, with where each is printed
ItemChargeWhere printed
General instrument$26.00 covers pages 1 to 15; $4.00 for every page past thatG.S. 161-10

Document outside the format standards$25.00 extraCounty recording page
Certified copy$5.00 for page one, $2.00 per later pageCounty records page
Plain copy25 cents a page, with $1.00 or a stamped envelope added by mailCounty records page

Plats are separate. A freestanding plat must be 18 by 24 inches on film or mylar and cleared by the county review officer, and the state schedule lists plats at $21.00 per sheet.

Who pays the Brunswick County excise tax?

The seller owes it. G.S. 105-228.30 makes the transferor pay the register before recording, at one dollar per $500 of value, counting any leftover fraction.

The county's records page lists earlier rates, including $0.50 and $0.55 per $500 for stretches between 1932 and 1991, which explains the different stamps on old deeds. Half of each collection stays in county government and half is sent on to the state.

A separate hurdle is unpaid property tax. The county names tax certification as a recording condition, and an electronically filed deed must state that any delinquent taxes will be paid to the county tax collector by the closing attorney when funds are disbursed. If back taxes are owed, request a payoff figure from the collector early, and have your attorney show the excise line on the settlement statement.

Can a lender or title firm e-record in Brunswick County?

Yes. Businesses and lending institutions can e-record through Internet Technologies, Inc. (Inttek) during the usual weekday recording hours. Private owners normally file on paper.

  • Card and PayPal payments add 6% of the document's total cost plus $0.50.
  • ACH funds moved into escrow add 2.5% of the amount escrowed.
  • Regular recording fees remain due on top of the vendor charge.
  • Maps can be e-recorded when they show an existing parcel.

An e-recorded deed must open with a prepared-by statement naming a North Carolina attorney and the delinquent tax wording, and every e-filing needs the submitter statement tied to the county's submitter agreement. Ask your closing firm which route it uses, because electronic filing is how many deeds reach the office the day they are signed.

How can I search Brunswick County deeds and get copies?

The county's online search covers filings from September 1939 forward. Fill in any one field, such as the buyer's name, a date range, a document type or a book and page, and each hit offers a PDF download.

Index books from 1932 to 1953 are scanned as legacy indexes, so you find the name alphabetically and then type the book and page into the search page. For a certified copy, mail a written request and payment to BCROD at the PO Box, or order through the search site.

Two protections are worth knowing. Anyone may ask the office to strip a Social Security number or bank or card number from an image shown online, using the redaction form. And the register offers a free fraud alert that sends a notice whenever a document is recorded under your name, which suits owners of vacant or inherited houses.

How is Brunswick County changing, according to the Census?

Growth is the story here. The Census Bureau estimated 174,702 people in July 2025, compared with 107,431 at the 2010 count and a 27.8% gain over the 2020 base. People 65 and older are 36.6% of the total. Housing units number 116,023 on 850.08 square miles of land.

The 2020 to 2024 survey puts the owner share at 84.6%, the middle home value at $349,800 and the middle household income at $77,024. Typical gross rent is $1,351. With 4,457 building permits in 2025, new construction keeps adding deeds to the office's workload.

Source: Census QuickFacts for Brunswick County.

Why does recording matter when I sell a Brunswick County house?

Recording sets the pecking order of claims. Under G.S. 47-18, an unregistered conveyance carries no weight against lien creditors or paying buyers, and priority runs by registration time.

For that reason a buyer's attorney keeps the funds back until the deed and new loan papers are filed. On your side, an old mortgage should show a recorded satisfaction. The lender files it, the county charges nothing, and a quick search of your own deed confirms it is there.

Inherited houses, liens and unpaid taxes slow the process, so raise them with the closing attorney early. A cash buyer's offer still needs the same deed, the same tax certification and the same excise payment.

More questions about Brunswick County, NC Register of Deeds

Where does a Brunswick County deed get filed?

At Building I, 75 Courthouse Drive NE, Bolivia, NC 28422, or by mail to PO Box 87. Recording hours are 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, and the phone is 910-253-2690.

How is the Brunswick County deed stamp tax figured?

The rate is $1.00 per $500 of value conveyed, a figure the county also words as $2 per $1,000, and the seller pays it up front.

What is the fee to file a mortgage in Brunswick County?

State law sets $64.00 through page 35 and $4.00 for each page beyond. Filing the satisfaction after payoff is free.

Can a homeowner e-record a Brunswick County deed?

Only businesses and lenders can, through Inttek. Vendor fees run 6% plus $0.50 for cards or 2.5% for ACH escrow, in addition to normal recording fees.

How do I order a certified deed copy from Bolivia?

Mail a written request with payment to BCROD at the PO Box, or click the request link in the online search results. Page one is $5.00 and later pages are $2.00 each.

Records themselves go back to the 1700s. Anyone who prefers paper can use the public record search room at the same address during those hours.

What documents does Buncombe County record?

The office keeps the paper trail for Buncombe land: conveyances, deeds of trust and their cancellations, plats, assumed business names, UCC filings, separation agreements, road maintenance agreements and powers of attorney. It is all open to public inspection.

The office describes itself as a record keeper. Staff will not draft or change papers, although forms for satisfactions and assumed names are on hand, and anyone needing a deed drawn up is sent to an attorney. Filings must be originals with live signatures and a notary's acknowledgment.

  • Real estate conveyances and deeds of trust

  • Plats and miscellaneous maps
  • Assumed names and UCC filings
  • Powers of attorney and related papers

How should a Buncombe County deed be formatted?

Start with paper size, which must be letter or legal. Leave a three-inch blank strip at the top of page one, half an inch on its other edges, and half an inch on every edge of later pages.

  • Black ink, white paper, a legible font of 9 points or bigger.
  • Printing on a single side of each sheet.
  • A title for the instrument written near the top of page one.
  • No highlighter over important information.
  • Color or grayscale images count as non-standard.

Off-standard deeds are accepted at an added $25. A color scan alone triggers it, so have the final deed printed on plain white paper.

What do filings and copies cost in Buncombe County?

Typical recording and copy charges at the College Street office

To order by mail, enclose the Real Estate Records Request Form and a check or money order made out to Register of Deeds. Adding a stamped return envelope speeds things up.

Who covers the deed tax when a Buncombe County home sells?

Responsibility rests with the seller, who pays the register before the deed is filed. The charge is one dollar on each $500 of price, counting a partial $500 as a whole one.

Buncombe keeps half in its general fund and passes the rest to the state monthly, net of refunds and the county's allowance. Review the excise tax line on the settlement statement, because it follows the price on the deed.

A parcel that straddles two counties pays in the one holding the larger share of its value.

Can documents be filed online in Buncombe County?

Yes, for firms. Lenders, law offices, attorneys and surveyors submit through an authorized eRecording provider.

After choosing a provider, the company completes a Submitter Memorandum of Understanding. For a seller this explains how a title firm can have a deed recorded quickly. Individual owners can carry originals to College Street or mail them.

Filed documents can be found in the online records search, which comes with a video tutorial. Results cover deeds, deeds of trust, powers of attorney and assumed names, and can be printed.

What online tools does Buncombe County offer for land records?

On its Real Estate Recording page, the county pairs an Online Records Search with a lookup tutorial, and nearby sit a Parcel Ownership Dashboard, a Cemetery Finder and a Farm Finder. The index runs from conveyances to assumed names, and the oldest entries date to the 1700s.

Use them before listing to verify how title is vested, notice an old easement or catch a deed of trust that was never cleared. Should one show up, contact the lender, who is the one to file the cancellation.

How does the 2026 reappraisal delay touch a Buncombe County sale?

Buncombe's 2026 tax bills use the 2021 schedule of values because of a state law passed in July 2026, and the new reappraisal takes effect January 1, 2027. The county levy on those bills is 61.54 cents for each $100 of valuation.

What a seller will notice is that the bill due around closing rests on the older values. Bills can be viewed at tax.buncombenc.gov, and the Tax Assessment office takes questions at 828-250-4920. The separate Buncombe tax guide on this site covers appeals, relief programs and rates.

What do the numbers say about Buncombe County housing?

The Census Bureau puts mid-2025 headcount at 277,417, which is 3.0% above the 2020 base, spread over 142,799 housing units. That works out to 410.4 people per square mile of the county's 656.50 land square miles.

Across 2020 through 2024, owners hold 66.2% of homes. The middle home is worth $391,800, the middle rent is $1,362 and the middle household brings in $74,436. Commutes average 21.1 minutes. Permits issued in 2025 numbered 2,028.

About a third of homes are rented, so some sellers are investors with tenants in place. A lease leaves the register's work unchanged, but your closing attorney should hear about it early.

Source: Census QuickFacts for Buncombe County.

What should I check in Asheville before my deed is recorded?

Three checks matter: the deed's layout, the excise line and any property tax still owed. G.S. 47-18 gives a conveyance force against lien creditors and buyers only after registration, so recording time sets priority.

An autumn closing can overlap a bill that has been issued but not paid, since bills normally come due September 1 and carry a grace period into early January. Collections answers at 828-250-4910.

Read your own deed in the online search before accepting an offer, including the legal description and easements. If a mortgage was paid off long ago, confirm a satisfaction was recorded, and ask the lender to file one when it was not.

More questions about Buncombe County, NC Register of Deeds

What hours does the Buncombe register keep?

It serves the public weekdays, 8 am to 5 pm, at 205 College Street. Holiday closings follow the county calendar posted on the office's web page.

Will the Buncombe register help draft my deed?

No. Its role is to record and preserve documents, not to write or revise them. Forms for satisfactions and assumed names are available, and deed drafting goes to an attorney.

How much is a certified copy of a Buncombe deed?

Page one of a certified copy is $5 and each later page is $2. Plain copies cost $0.25 a page. Mail orders should enclose payment made out to Register of Deeds.

How much is the Buncombe County deed tax?

The rate is $1.00 on each $500 of price, with any remainder counted as a full $500 unit. The seller settles it before recording, and the county retains half.

What if my Buncombe County deed is not on standard paper?

The deed is recorded, with a $25 non-standard fee on top. Standard means letter or legal paper, black ink, at least 9 point type and the required margins.

Chatham County by the numbers

Where is the Chatham County Register of Deeds?

You will find it inside the Courthouse Annex, 12 East Street, Pittsboro, ground-level wing, facing the traffic circle where the historic Superior Courthouse stands. Parking is behind the annex and is reached from Chatham Street, which is also US 15/501 South, just past the circle. From the lot, walk to the wide stairwell opening in the middle of the building, skip the stairs, and take the passage on the left to the end of the building nearest the BP station.

Letters go to P.O. Box 756, Pittsboro, NC 27312, while couriers use the East Street address. The main number is 919-542-8235.

Chatham posts three clocks, and a closing that slips past the earlier ones will wait until the next business day.

  • Counter open: eight in the morning until five in the evening on weekdays.
  • Paper documents accepted for recording until 4:30 p.m.
  • Electronic submissions accepted from 8:00 a.m. through 4:00 p.m.

The office closes on state holidays. Its 2026 closing list ends with Thursday and Friday, November 26 and 27, then December 24, 25 and 28.

What does Chatham charge to put a deed on record?

The base price for a deed is $26.00 covering 15 pages, then $4.00 per extra page, and the office notes a $2 verification fee is folded into that amount. A mortgage-style deed of trust is $64 for the first 35 pages with the same $4 per extra page. The table below repeats the real estate items from the county's own fee list.

Land record charges listed on the Pittsboro office's fee page
ItemFee
General instrument$26.00 through page 15, then $4.00 a page
Deed$26.00 through page 15, then $4.00 a page
Deed of trust$64 through page 35, then $4 a page
Release of a deed of trustNo fee
Plat of land$21.00
Certified copy of land records$5 first page, $2 each added page
Uncertified copies of records25 cents per page
Extra instrument inside one document$10.00 each

These match the statewide schedule in G.S. 161-10, which also makes a nonstandard document cost $25.00 extra. The county lists a uniform commercial code filing at $38.00 for one or two pages. Fees are collected before a document is filed.

Can a Chatham County deed be filed online?

Electronic filing runs through two vendors, Simplifile and CSC, and the office takes those submissions Monday to Friday until 4:00 p.m. The office says it now e-records plats as well. Closing attorneys and title companies can submit through those vendors, which means a seller often never carries the deed to the office.

CSC lists erecording@cscglobal.com and 1-866-652-0111 for questions about its service. A paper filing needs original documents, and the county notes that the register of deeds is a depository of records, not a creator of documents or a fixer of mistakes. Staff cannot draft or correct a deed for you.

Online searching is separate. The county's remote access site, chathamncrod.org, lets you look up recorded deeds, and the same office offers an e-mail alert if a document with a chosen name is ever filed. An owner worried about deed fraud can sign up through that site.

What formatting rules can get a Chatham County deed rejected?

Anything filed after July 1, 2002 must follow the page layout in G.S. 161-14(b), which the county reprints. A document that misses a rule still gets recorded, but the office first collects a $25.00 nonstandard fee, so clean formatting saves money. The county lists these requirements.

  • Letter or legal sheets only.
  • Leave three empty inches above the first line of page one; every other edge needs a quarter inch of white space.
  • Dark print on white stock, one side only, with type no smaller than 9 points.
  • The kind of instrument (for example, warranty deed) labeled under the blank top band.
  • A prepared-by line on the first page of any deed or deed of trust, kept out of the margin zones.
  • Who gets the original back, with a mailing address, on the first page of every paper filing.

Pen is acceptable for blanks on printed forms and for corrections.

How does the deed excise tax work in Chatham County?

Each $500 of price, or fraction of $500, carries $1.00 of tax, which the seller hands to the office ahead of recording under G.S. 105-228.30. The county general fund keeps half and the state revenue department receives the balance. The closing attorney deducts it from the seller's proceeds and sends it with the recording package, so look for it as a line on the settlement statement.

Order of filing matters. G.S. 47-18 says a conveyance gives no shield against later buyers or lien creditors until the register of deeds in the land's county has it on file; priority follows the clock time of filing. In practice, a buyer's lender wants the deed logged before any other filing against the house.

Local numbers show what flows through this counter. QuickFacts lists 38,294 housing units for mid-2025 and 517 building permits in 2025, plus a $446,200 median home value for 2020 to 2024 (Census QuickFacts). With values that high, the per-$500 tax is a bigger line item on a Chatham closing than in many counties, and sellers should budget for it before listing.

What other services does the Chatham County Register of Deeds offer?

Beyond land records, the office is the keeper of births, deaths and marriages for the county, and it files notary oaths and assumed-name records. Marriage licenses and notary oaths are by appointment only, and the line for appointments is the same 919-542-8235.

Certified copies of birth and death records are $10.00 each, and a marriage license is $60.00. These records matter to sellers more often than people expect: an heir selling a parent's house may need a certified death certificate to give the title company, and a divorce or marriage can change who must sign the deed. Request certified copies early, because the office cannot hand over a record to someone who is not eligible under state law.

The register of deeds also runs an alert service for document fraud, covered above, which is useful to any owner who is about to sell and wants to know if anything unexpected is filed under the family name.

What should a Chatham County seller do before the deed is recorded?

Settle property tax, gather the paperwork and let the closing office handle recording. Chatham reappraises on a four-year cycle and kept its county rate at 60 cents per $100 for fiscal year 2026-27, so the tax figure on a settlement statement may differ from the older bill you remember. Our Chatham County property tax guide covers the offices, appeals and relief programs.

A seller with a deed of trust should ask the lender for a payoff and expect a cancellation to be recorded afterward at no fee. A seller with a plat issue, an old easement or a missing signature on an inherited parcel should raise it early, since the register of deeds will not repair a defect.Ask a North Carolina attorney how to fix a title defect before you list.

More questions about Chatham County, NC Register of Deeds

What number reaches the Pittsboro recording desk?

Dial 919-542-8235. Staff there can answer questions about filing a package, and the physical office is at 12 East Street with a mailing box at P.O. Box 756.

What is the latest I can bring a paper deed to the Chatham counter?

Half past four, on business days. Electronic filings cut off earlier, at four, and holidays on the state calendar mean no recording at all.

What is the fee for an ordinary deed?

Budget $26.00 for a short deed of up to fifteen pages, with $4.00 more for every added page. The excise tax paid by the seller is a different charge.

What if my deed ignores the layout rules?

The office will accept it and add $25.00 for a nonstandard document under G.S. 161-10(a)(19). Fix the top band and print dark on white before you submit.

Which electronic vendors does Chatham work with?

Simplifile and CSC. Both feed the register of deeds on weekdays up to 4:00 p.m., and plats can now go in electronically too.

One in three residents (33.7%) is 65 or older, and the county saw 239 building permits in 2025. Older owners may hold property tax relief that changes when a house sells, which is covered below.

Fifteen pages of a deed cost $26 and thirty-five pages of a deed of trust cost $64, with $4 charged on each page beyond those counts. The office's posted schedule follows, in the office's own wording.

The county page notes that plats filed since October 1991 must be on mylar transparent plastic in 18 by 24, 21 by 30 or 24 by 36 inch sizes. Certified birth, death and marriage certificates are $10 each. The recording numbers line up with the uniform schedule in G.S. 161-10, and that statute lists no fee for recording a cancellation of a deed of trust.

How do deed stamps work in Cherokee County?

Stamps appear on the county page at $2 per $1,000 of purchase price, matching the statute's $1.00 for each $500 slice. G.S. 105-228.30 makes the transferor responsible, with payment due to the register ahead of filing. One half supports the county's general fund and the other half goes to Raleigh.

What this means for a seller in the county:

  • Look for the stamp tax among the seller's charges.
  • The statute counts every $500 of price or fractional part of $500, so an uneven price rounds up to the next step.
  • Options, contracts to convey and leases longer than three years only bind later purchasers and lien creditors after registration where the land sits, per G.S. 47-18.

Where can I see Cherokee County tax and deed information?

The county's interactive tax viewer shows tax amounts from 2008 forward and refreshes itself each morning at 6 a.m., so a payment shows up the next day. First comes a disclaimer: the data was built for the county's internal use from recorded deeds and plats, and users are told to verify against the public records.

Questions about the data go to the Cherokee County Appraisal Office at 828-835-3296. That office is the one to call about a value, a parcel record or a mismatch between the tax viewer and a deed. For the deed itself, the register of deeds in Murphy keeps the original recorded copy, and a certified copy costs $5 for the first page and $2 for each page after that.

Older, disabled and veteran owners file relief requests locally with the county assessor. For 2026, owners 65 or older (or disabled) with income no higher than $38,800 can exclude the larger of $25,000 or half the appraised value, while the disabled veteran exclusion shields the first $45,000. Owners apply on form AV-9, and filings are taken up to June 1 ahead of the tax year. A seller already receiving one of these benefits should ask the Appraisal Office how a sale affects it. The statutes are G.S. 105-277.1 and G.S. 105-277.1C.

What else does the Cherokee County register handle for homeowners?

The office also keeps vital records and issues marriage licenses, and a few of those charges come up around a home sale. A death certificate may be needed by heirs, a marriage license or certificate can bear on who signs a deed, and a notary appointment is available for $10.

  • Certified birth, death and marriage certificates are $10 each; the county directs requests through its vital records portal.
  • A marriage license is $60.
  • Notary appointments are $10 each.
  • Copies of any record are $0.10 apiece.

These items follow the county's price list. If heirs need a certified certificate, order it early so the title company has it when the file is reviewed.

What should a Cherokee County seller prepare before recording?

Sort out the tax bill, the payoff and the title work first, then let the closing attorney file. Bills fall due September 1 and start accruing interest on January 6 under G.S. 105-360. These steps help a sale go smoothly.

  • Confirm every owner on the chain of title, including heirs on an inherited house.
  • Ask a surveyor about plats if the lot lines are unclear, since a plat is a separate $21 filing.
  • Collect payoff letters for any deed of trust; the register records the release at no charge.
  • Pull your own vesting deed so the legal description in the new deed matches it word for word.

A register of deeds records documents but does not draft them, so hire a North Carolina attorney for the deed. If repairs, liens or disagreeing heirs have stalled a sale, a cash purchase avoids a lender's schedule; our North Carolina page explains that route.

From 2020 to 2024 the typical owned home was valued at $232,300, the typical household earned $53,628 and gross rent had a middle point of $813, all per Census QuickFacts. The poverty rate is 15.4%. The county counts 13,241 households of 2.20 people each, and 89.5% of residents kept the same address from the prior year.

Those figures point to settled owners and moderate prices. Owners pay a median of $1,242 a month with a mortgage and $376 without. For a seller, the $2 per $1,000 stamp is a modest charge beside the equity in a typical house, although it grows with the price.

The same QuickFacts table counts 2,522 veterans for 2020 to 2024, which is relevant because the disabled veteran exclusion has no age or income cap. Commutes average 25.2 minutes, and 49.2% of people 16 or older are working or looking for work.

It is at 75 Peachtree Street, Suite 126-A, Murphy, NC 28906. Call 828-837-2613 to reach the register, and bring land records in by 4:30 p.m.

The county lists $26 for a deed up to 15 pages, then $4 a page. Deeds of trust are $64 up to 35 pages, and a plat filing is $21.

The county prints the stamp as $2 for each $1,000 of price, which is the same rate the state writes as $1.00 per $500. Sellers pay it when the deed goes on record.

The Cherokee County Appraisal Office, at 828-835-3296, takes questions about the parcel data in the county's tax viewer.

Is there a charge for deed copies?

Yes. Ordinary copies run ten cents a page, while a certified document is $5 for page one and $2 per page afterward. Vital record certificates are $10 each.

Where is the Chowan County Register of Deeds?

Its own mission statement calls the office the custodian of vital records and real estate recordings. Its archive of real estate material reaches back to the 1600s, marriage licenses are dated as early as 1868, and birth and death records were not required to be recorded until 1913. For sellers, that depth means a title search here can run through very old deeds.

Census QuickFacts shows 14,082 residents in July 2025 on 172.66 square miles of land, down from 14,793 at the 2010 census and up 2.7% from the 2020 base. There are 7,312 housing units, and permits numbered just 48 for 2025, so most deeds here move existing houses and land.

What must be done before a deed is recorded in Chowan County?

Chowan's pre-recording checklist adds a local land transfer tax, a parcel number and a tax office stop. The recording page spells out each requirement, and the table below follows the office's own order.

Pre-recording checklist from the Edenton office
RequirementWhat the county page says

Every document must also be dated and carry a legal description. Deeds with an attached survey, and other surveys, must be reviewed and signed by the county's review officer before recording.

Does Chowan County have a land transfer tax on top of the state excise tax?

Yes. The county's checklist adds a land transfer tax of 1% of the sale price, citing S.L. 1985-881, alongside the excise tax. The excise tax is the state levy, which the statute (G.S. 105-228.30) writes as $1.00 per $500 and the county writes as $2.00 per $1,000, to be paid by the transferor before the deed goes on record.

Both charges scale with the price. Do not estimate either from memory: ask the register of deeds or your closing attorney for the current figure and for how it is split on your contract. On the checklist, payment of both is a precondition to recording.

Where do Chowan County deeds go before they reach the register of deeds?

Two county offices touch a deed first. The Land Records/GIS Department approves a parcel identification number for any real estate document with a legal description, including plats, and its review officer signs off on surveys. The department is in the courthouse at 101 S. Broad Street and takes calls at (252) 482-7157.

The Chowan County Tax Office is the second stop, and it is a step many sellers miss. All deeds must be presented there with an affidavit of consideration before the register of deeds will record. The tax office is at 305 W. Freemason Street, Edenton, with a phone number of (252) 482-8486 and a mailing address of PO Box 1030.

A sensible order is below.

  1. Have the deed drafted by an attorney with the drafter's name, the grantee's mailing address and a legal description.
  2. Get the parcel number approved by Land Records/GIS, plus review of any attached survey.
  3. Take the deed and an affidavit of consideration to the tax office.
  4. Pay the recording fee, excise tax and transfer tax at the register of deeds, and record.

A closing attorney normally handles these steps, but a seller who is giving a deed to a family member or buyer without one will need to do them personally.

Which Whiteville office records Columbus County deeds, and until when?

Deeds for Columbus County land go to Suite B at 125 Washington Street in Whiteville. Mail goes to PO Box 1086, ZIP 28472. Doors open at 8:30 each weekday morning and close at 5:00 in the afternoon, apart from county holidays.

Plan around the filing cutoff. Intake for recording ends at 4:45 p.m. every day, a quarter hour before closing time. Marriage license applications close even earlier, at 4:30 p.m.

A home seller meets this office at the very end, since the deed that transfers title and the buyer's lender's deed of trust are both filed here. The closing attorney or title office usually carries the paper over, so your part is mostly knowing the cutoff when you read a closing calendar.

What does a Columbus County deed cost to file?

A flat $26.00 covers the first fifteen pages of an ordinary deed, and each page beyond that adds $4.00. The county's fee notice cites G.S. 161-10, the uniform schedule used by every register of deeds in the state.

The seller owes it, and the register collects before filing. State law prices the tax at one dollar per $500 of price or value, rounding a partial $500 up (G.S. 105-228.30). The county's own FAQ words the same rate as $2 per thousand dollars of purchase price.

Half of the money goes into the county's general fund and the state revenue department takes the rest. Since the tax follows price, expect a separate line on the settlement statement, and get the number from your closing attorney before signing day.

Register staff cannot quote the tax on a given sale without the deed in hand. Changing names on title takes a fresh deed, filed at the standard $26.00 rate. The office suggests an attorney for drafting and warns that excise tax may also apply.

Can I record or search Columbus County land records online?

Yes. The county accepts electronic recording of every document type except plats, and a list of approved vendors is on the e-recording page of the register's website. Electronic filing lets a closing package reach the office before the 4:45 p.m. cutoff without anyone driving to Whiteville.

The online index is name based. It decides who wins when two claims compete for the same land. A deed, option, lease past three years or right of first refusal protects its holder against lien creditors and paying buyers only from the moment of registration in the land's home county (G.S. 47-18). The earlier registration ranks first.

That rule is why a signed deed alone does not finish a sale. Until the Columbus County register stamps it with a recording time, a later claim could still jump ahead.

Owner financing follows the same logic. Chapter 47H reaches a one to four family home sold on five or more payments while the seller keeps title. Recording falls to the seller, who has five business days to file the contract or a memorandum of it. The buyer also gets a three business day window to back out. Read the whole chapter before choosing that route.

What farmland notice appears on Columbus County land records?

Session Law 2018-113, quoted on the county tax office page, requires land records to warn title researchers when a tract lies within half a mile of a qualifying poultry, swine or dairy farm, within 600 feet of any other qualifying farm, or within half a mile of a voluntary agricultural district.

A buyer's title search may therefore flag your parcel. The statute adds that no cause of action arises from a researcher's failure to report it, and that real estate brokers and appraisers are not liable for omitting it. It is a notice, not a restriction on the sale. With 938.12 square miles of land and roughly 54 people per square mile (Census, 2020), farm neighbors are common, so expect the question and answer it early.

  • Residents 65 and older: 22.2%.

With 55 permits in 2025 and a population below its 2010 level, new construction is thin. Price your expectations against the $146,000 median, and ask your closing attorney which county records to pull before you list.

How do property taxes fit into a Columbus County sale?

County tax bills fall due September 1. The tax office takes payment by mail, phone, drop box and at the counter, and online through columbus.webtaxpay.com. Its mailing box is PO Box 1468 in Whiteville.

A bill stays at face value until early January. From January 6 a 2% charge applies through the end of January, and from February 1 three-fourths of one percent is added per month or part of a month (G.S. 105-360). The lien for real property tax attaches as of the date property is listed under G.S. 105-285 (G.S. 105-355), so the seller's bill follows the parcel into the sale.

Get a payoff figure from the tax office ahead of closing and hand it to whoever drafts the settlement statement. The same office lists staff for senior citizen exemptions. The statute's "transferor," meaning the seller, owes it, and the office collects before it records anything. Revenue is then shared evenly between the county and the state. What must a deed show before the Cumberland County office will accept it?

  • A return address block, also on page one.

Statewide, the bill is due September 1, interest starts January 6 at two percent, with three-quarters of a percent added for each month from February 1 on. A veteran with a permanent, total, service-connected disability rating may apply to the county assessor for the state exclusion, which removes $45,000 from the appraised value.

  • The county counts 129,758 households averaging 2.48 people.
  • Veterans number 40,226.
  • Median household income is $61,291, in 2024 dollars.

What should a Cumberland County seller check ahead of signing?

Begin with the mortgage. Filing a satisfaction of a paid-off loan costs nothing, so a cleared mortgage should end with that document on record. If payments have lapsed, the lender uses a power-of-sale case heard by the clerk of superior court, and once a sale is reported anyone may file an upset bid within ten days, at least five percent above the price and no less than $750.00 higher.

Next, study the title. Pull the last recorded deed, look for liens, and check whether a deed of trust remains open. A house that came through an estate also warrants a look at the clerk's estates division records. A sale that skips repairs may trim the to-do list, though the deed, excise tax and filing fee are still due.

Who pays the deed excise tax when selling a house in Cumberland County?

The seller pays, and the statute calls that party the transferor. It is handed over at the counter before the deed is filed. The county page prints $2.00 against each $1,000 of price, and the statute prints $1.00 against each $500.

What does Cumberland County charge to file a deed?

Can the Register of Deeds help me write a deed?

No. The office says state law forbids its staff from advising on legal questions or writing deeds. A deed must be drafted, signed and notarized before it is brought in, and an attorney can answer wording questions.

Yes, it costs nothing: an email reaches you whenever someone files paper carrying your name in Fayetteville. Sign up at ccrod.org under Records Search. The office calls it an early warning, with no guarantee against fraud.

Where do I send a Cumberland County real property listing form?

Mail it to Tax Administration, Attn: Real Estate Division, P.O. Box 449, Fayetteville, NC 28302, or bring it to Room 530 of the courthouse. The county asks for forms by January 31 so changes reach that year's assessment.

Real estate searches are done online through the county's deeds search site, and records there are indexed from 1984 to the present. For anything earlier than 1984, the office asks you to contact staff directly.

  • When looking for a satisfaction of a mortgage, search under the document type Release.
  • Judgments are looked up through the Clerk of Courts office instead.

What is the Davidson County tax certification rule for deeds?

Beginning March 1, 2019, the counter turns away any real property deed lacking a certificate from the Tax Administrator that no overdue tax is attached to the parcel. The county adopted the requirement by commissioner resolution on August 14, 2018, under G.S. 161-31.

An attorney-supervised closing offers a way around the certificate. The deed instead carries a printed line saying a North Carolina attorney prepared it and that any overdue tax will be sent to the collector out of the sale money. Without an attorney, you request a certificate from the Tax Department through its online form, and the county warns that a certificate can take up to two business days. Since March 1, 2019, the office accepts a real property deed only with a Tax Administrator certificate showing no delinquent taxes, or under a closing attorney who agrees to pay any delinquent taxes from the proceeds. The certificate can take up to two business days.
